problems_checked.P1: Confirmed Major by independently checking the exact analytic infinite family. For every prime p>7, c=7p is square-free, a0 is allowed, and CRT choices make q1,q2,b2,b3 units. Modulo7 the five global exception expressions are -1,-p,5p,p,-2p, all nonzero, so the asserted generic branch applies. The actual source inverse bars and unconjugated product were visually verified. CRT scales both Kloosterman arguments by inverse complementary moduli and yields C=K*D_p with fixed K=C(0,2,1,1,7,1,2). At p, q1=q2=1, the change of variable gives D_p=sum_(z!=z_p)S(1,z;p)^2=p(p-1)-S(1,z_p;p)^2. Reality follows from conjugation and x->-x; additive-character orthogonality gives the second moment exactly. The least nonzero minimizer has square<p, so D_p>p^2-2p. K is a sum of216 seventh roots with integer multiplicities; vanishing would force all seven multiplicities equal, impossible since7 does not divide216. The retained exact histogram is corroborating evidence, not a floating asymptotic argument. Thus the ratio to c^(3/2+epsilon) diverges for each0<epsilon<1/2. All stated assumptions, including the stronger unit interpretation, hold. Publisher p46 directly invokes this uniform estimate in(9.22); the same claim and use persist in separately checked arXiv v3 pp51 and36. This is a false core arithmetic input, not an exhibited GL(3) L-function or final-subconvexity counterexample. The full residue family has not been embedded into every dyadic size restriction. A sufficient primewise-degeneracy replacement and its propagation/final exponent remain unverified, so easy textual changes do not justify downgrading the core defect.
